pr_body:
This PR follows https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/64212, further refactoring the bake code of `Curve3D`. 

The main change is to calculate tangent directly from bezier curve, without going
through discretized polyline.

This is mathematically correct method has the following benefits:
1. More accurate transform frames sampling along the curve; 
2. Path3DFollow movement is completely smooth, fixing https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/64212#discussion_r1020716713;
3. Initial up vector is not influenced by baking interval, fixing https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/68893
4. Adhoc checks and fixes become unnecessary, leading to simpler and more performant code.

The same refactor can be applied to `Curve2D` in a seperate PR.

_Production edit: Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/68893_

issue_context.title: Curve3D::sample_baked_up_vector() returns value perpendicular to its previous value after merge
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

8ab3e73a799bbfa862403747a5de9fc96ba83149

### System information

Ubuntu 22.04

### Issue description

Prior to 8ab3e73a799bbfa862403747a5de9fc96ba83149, `Curve3D::sample_baked_up_vector()` returned a somewhat plausible up vector for some curves, however since 8ab3e73a799bbfa862403747a5de9fc96ba83149 it returns a vector perpendicular to the old value. Original PR #64212

The simple attached project displays the angle between the first curve point up vector, and the global up vector

8ab3e73a799bbfa862403747a5de9fc96ba83149

![2022-11-19-102053_1916x1033_scrot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18740/202861009-b4a0f887-f355-4bc6-9d04-2b9690a524fa.png)

8ab3e73a799bbfa862403747a5de9fc96ba83149^

![2022-11-19-103036_1916x1033_scrot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18740/202861365-66b2968f-c756-44a9-b195-10ea60153a90.png)

Additional screenshots here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/64212#issuecomment-1320811390 (more difficult to reproduce because it requires rebasing another change)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Node3D
2. Assign it a Curve3D
3. call `Curve3D::sample_baked_up_vector()`
4. Observe the value with Godot after 8ab3e73a799bbfa862403747a5de9fc96ba83149
5. Observe the value with Godot 8ab3e73a799bbfa862403747a5de9fc96ba83149^

Run the attached project to accomplish the same

### Minimal reproduction project

Run the example scene in this project to show this behavior [Curve3D Up Vector Test.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10047493/Curve3D.Up.Vector.Test.zip)
comments:
I thought I'd also note in the original PR there was quite a bit of discussion about whether or not the up vector is naturally a property of Curve3D or if it belongs elsewhere. I'm not sure any conclusions were reached but it obviously has a bearing on whether `Curve3D::sample_baked_up_vector()` should exist at all.

The `sample_baked_with_rotation()` method which @xiongyaohua added in that PR is more useful than `sample_baked_up_vector()` anyway, every use of `sample_baked_up_vector()` that I can think of is ultimately trying to establish a basis for some transform anyway. Perhaps the real fix is to simply drop the `sample_baked_up_vector()` method entirely.

Sorry for the late reply, as I am occupied by other things recently. I'll investigate this week.

Should be fixed by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/69043

review_comments: Is there any reason to exist the two tessellate functions? Since they seem to be doing almost the same thing, I think it is enough to remain one of the two as `tesselate()`, and rename `_tessellate_even_length()` to `_tesselate()`.

The both tessellate bezier curve into points, but in very different ways. 

- The original `tesselate()` produce dense points near corners, and sparse points at straight parts. This way the curve can be approximated with minimal number of points.
- The `tesselate_even_length()` produce points with almost even density no matter at corners or straight segments. This even density make some processing easier.

I think both behavior have its use case and both can be exposed. If you insist on keep one public `tesselate()` method, how about we  do this?

1. rename current `tesselate()` to `_tessellate_adaptive_length()`, as an internal method.
2. add an `mode` parameter to the public method `tesselate`, which specify whether to call `_tessellate_adaptive_length` or `_tesselate_even_length` internally.
